answer: Yes, Medicare can cover daily skilled nursing visits for insulin when your father is physically or mentally unable to self-inject and there is no other person able and willing to inject him. The passages do not state how long daily visits can continue or how to arrange scheduling.

citations.quote: The exception to the intermittent requirement is daily skilled nursing services for diabetics unable to administer their insulin (when there is no able and willing caregiver).

where a patient is either physically or mentally unable to self-inject insulin and there is no other person who is able and willing to inject the patient, the injections would be considered a reasonable and necessary skilled nursing service.

gold_answer: Yes. Daily skilled nursing to give insulin to a diabetic who cannot self-administer it, when there is no able and willing caregiver, is the stated exception to the intermittent requirement. Otherwise intermittent usually means a skilled nursing need at least once every 60 days.
gold_quote: In most instances, this definition will be met if a patient requires a skilled nursing service at least once every 60 days. The exception to the intermittent requirement is daily skilled nursing services for diabetics unable to administer their insulin (when there is no able and willing caregiver).

judge.rationale: The answer correctly says daily skilled nursing for insulin is covered when the patient cannot self-inject and no able and willing caregiver exists, and both claims appear in P1 and P3, though it leaves out the gold's non-essential 60-day context.

question: My father is diabetic and cannot give himself insulin, and there is nobody else to do it. Can Medicare send a nurse every day?
